newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wind change increases Australian bushfires threat.
newsitem.headline: Wind change increases Australian bushfires threat.

text.p: Emergency services fighting huge bushfires near the southern city of Melbourne on Tuesday hold grave concerns about an emerging cold front that is forcing winds fuelling the blazes toward more densely populated areas.

"We've got three fires which are causing concern. With south westerly winds...this will tend to make those fires become very active on their eastern flanks," Country Fire Authority spokesman Ian Hamilton told Reuters.

Fire authorities said about 700 firefighters were battling three major blazes and several smaller ones that had razed 20 homes and destroyed forest in the Dandenong mountain range about 30 km (19 miles) east of Melbourne.
Police said the fires had forced the evacuation of more than 400 people from the area.
Hamilton said one fire near the township of Upwey would become particularly threatening with the wind change.
"This (wind change) would put it facing a heavily populated area and evacuation has been underway there for some time," he said.

Hamilton said two other major fires burning west and south-east of Melbourne mostly had been contained but not before one forced firefighters had to run for their lives as flames engulfed their water tanker.
He said there had been no serious injuries reported so far.

Melbourne has been suffering sweltering conditions since Saturday. Organisers at the Australian Open tennis tournament on Tuesday took the unprecedented step of closing the retractable roof on the centre after players said they feared for their health after playing in the extreme heat.
The player's fears rose after court temperatures soared to 50 degrees (122 degrees Fahrenheit) on Sunday and Monday.
The heatwave has prompted one Melbourne public swimming pool to stay open for 24 hours to meet a surge in demand.
It is not known what caused the fires.
National communications carrier Telstra Corp said its triple-zero emergency telephone lines had been jammed with calls about the fires.
